# Introduction

![Figure 1: SMS Message](SMSMessagePhoto.png){width=35% fig-align="center"}

Now we've all been there. After all, who can say no to a **FREE** $1,000? Just click the link! 

In all reality, you probably shouldn't click the link, as this is yet another SMS spam message. SMS (Short Message Service) spam messages are unsolicited texts--messages that recipients did not authroize to receive--that are sent in bulk to a large number of mobile phones. While often persuasive, deceptive, and sometimes indistinguishable from legitimate messages (like "Hi, I wanted to check up on you."), SMS spam messages can be more than an annoyance; they can also pose serious digital security risks. But what exactly makes a message spam? And how can we better understand the language used in spam messages to distinguish them from legitmate texts? 

These are the questions this project seeks to tackle.

# Data & Data Source

The SMS Spam Collection dataset contains 5,572 tagged SMS messages that have been collected for the purpose of SMS Spam research. Each message in the dataset is tagged as either ham--a legitmate message--or spam, to distinguish between the message types. 

The dataset used in this project was downloaded from [Kaggle](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/uciml/sms-spam-collection-dataset); however, the original dataset was obtained from the UC Irvine Machine Learning Repository and can be found at the citation below:

Almeida, Tiago and Jos Hidalgo. "SMS Spam Collection." UCI Machine Learning Repository, 2011, https://doi.org/10.24432/C5CC84.

```{r}
# Import dataset

library(tidyverse)
library(stringi)
library(patchwork)
library(ggmosaic)
library(scales)

sms <- read_csv("spam.csv")

sms <- sms |> 
    select("v1", "v2") |> 
    rename(Label = v1, Message = v2)

# Original dataset includes characters that R does not recongize, so let's change all such character to '`' which has no instances in the original dataset

sms <- sms |> 
    mutate(Message = iconv(Message, from = "", to = "UTF-8", sub = "`"), Label = factor(Label, levels = c("spam", "ham")))
```

# Part 1: Exploring SMS Spam Dataset

```{r}
#| fig-width: 12.5
#| fig-height: 6.25

# From dataset, how many messages are ham vs spam?

sms_bar <- sms |> 
    ggplot(aes(x = Label)) +
    geom_bar(aes(fill = Label)) +
    labs(title = "Number of Observations Per Message Type", x = "Message Type", y = "Count") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16), axis.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14), axis.text = element_text(size = 13), legend.position = "none")

# Let's visualize message length (includes spaces) per message type

sms_box <- sms |> 
    ggplot(aes(x = Label, y = str_length(Message))) +
    geom_boxplot(aes(color = Label), alpha = 0.5) +
    labs(title = "Distribution of Message Length Per Message Type", x = "Message Type", y = "Length of Message") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16), axis.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14), axis.text = element_text(size = 13), legend.position = "none")

sms_bar | sms_box

# Let's find the median message length for each message type

sms |> 
    group_by(Label) |> 
    summarize(Median = median(str_length(Message)))

# Median Length of Message for ham: 52 Characters
# Median length of Message for spam: 149 Characters

```

From the bar chart on the left, we observe that in the SMS Spam dataset, there are less than 1,000 messages that are spam while all other messages are ham (legitmate messages). Now, when analzying message lengths per message type from the boxplot on the right, we observe that spam messages have a higher median (149 characters) than ham messages (52 characters). Moreover, we also observe that for spam message the distribution of message lengths is less variable and less wide than with ham messages. 

# Part 2: Characterizing Spam Message Language

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 12

sms_words <- sms |> 
    mutate(Message = str_to_lower(Message)) |> 
    mutate(
        Free = str_detect(Message, "\\bfree\\b"),
        Win = str_detect(Message, "\\bwin\\b | \\bwon\\b"),
        Claim = str_detect(Message, "\\bclaim\\b"),
        Urgent = str_detect(Message, "\\burgent\\b"),
        Prize = str_detect(Message, "\\bprize\\b"),
        Call = str_detect(Message, "\\bcall\\b"),
        Now = str_detect(Message, "\\bnow\\b"),
        Reply = str_detect(Message, "\\breply\\b"),
        Congrats = str_detect(Message, "\\bcongrats\\b | \\bcongratulation(s)?\\b"),
        Activate = str_detect(Message, "\\bactivate\\b"),
        Private = str_detect(Message, "\\bprivate\\b"),
        Cash = str_detect(Message, "\\bcash\\b"),
        XXX = str_detect(Message, "\\bxxx\\b")
    ) 

sms_word <- pivot_longer(sms_words, Free:XXX, names_to = "Word", values_to = "Contains")

sms_word |> 
    filter(Contains) |> 
    count(Label, Word) |> 
    ggplot() +
    geom_mosaic(aes(x = Word, fill = Label, weight = n)) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0,1, by = 0.10)) +
    labs(title = "Proportion of Popular Spam Words by Message Type", subtitle = str_wrap("Each side column's widths on the y-axis represents the relative frequency of that word, while the colored areas show the proporation of messages containing the word per message type.", width = 100), y = "Proporation of Messages", fill = "Message Type") +
    coord_flip() +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16), plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 14), axis.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14), axis.text = element_text(size = 13))

```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 12.5
#| fig-height: 6.25


sms_duplicates <- sms |> 
    mutate(Message = str_to_lower(Message)) |>
    mutate(
        Exclam = str_count(Message, "!"),
        Money = str_count(Message, "\\$"),
        Free = str_count(Message, "\\bfree\\b"),
        Win = str_count(Message, "\\bwin\\b"),
        Cash = str_count(Message, "\\bcash\\b"),
        Call = str_count(Message, "\\bcall\\b"),
        Prize = str_count(Message, "\\bprize\\b")
    )

sms_dups <- sms_duplicates |> 
    pivot_longer(Exclam:Prize, names_to = "Expression", values_to = "Contains")


sms_dup_viz <- sms_dups |> 
    group_by(Label, Expression) |> 
    summarize(Mean_Repeats = mean(Contains)) |> 
    mutate(Expression = fct_relevel(factor(Expression), c("Exclam", "Call", "Free", "Prize", "Cash", "Win", "Money"))) |> 
    ggplot(aes(x = Mean_Repeats, y = Expression)) +
    geom_line() +
    geom_point(aes(color = Label), size = 4) +
    coord_flip() +
    labs(title = str_wrap("Difference in Mean Number of Repeats for Selected Words and Symbols Across Message Types", width = 80), x = "Mean Number of Repeats Per Message", color = "Message Type") +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0,1, by = 0.10)) +
    scale_y_discrete(labels = c("Exclam" = "!", "Money" = "$")) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16), axis.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14), axis.text = element_text(size = 13))

sms_dup_viz

```


```{r}
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 8

sms_moneys <- sms |> 
    mutate(Message = str_to_lower(Message)) |> 
    mutate(
        Pounds = parse_number(str_extract(Message, "\\d{0,3},?\\d{1,3}(?= pounds)")),
        Money = parse_number(str_extract(Message, "(?<=\\$)\\d{0,3},?\\d{1,3}")),
        Prize = parse_number(str_extract(Message, "\\d{0,3},?\\d{1,3}(?= prize)"))
    ) |> 
    pivot_longer(Pounds:Prize, names_to = "Expression", values_to = "Number")
    
sms_money_viz <- sms_moneys |> 
    ggplot(aes(x = Number, y = Expression, color = Label)) +
    geom_jitter(width = 0, height = 0.3, size = 2) +
    scale_x_log10(labels = label_comma()) +
    scale_y_discrete(labels = c("Money" = "$")) +
    labs(title = "Distribution of Monetary Values Used in Messages By Selected Expressions", subtitle = "Each Expression either precedes or follows each montary value.", x = "Monetary Value", color = "Message Type") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16), plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 14), axis.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14), axis.text = element_text(size = 13))

sms_money_viz

```
